answer: Monotonic counter equivocation proofs. Each identity signs every action with a secure-element key and a strictly increasing counter. If a copied key signs two different payloads at the same counter, the signed pair is public evidence; nodes reject that identity and all clones. Gossip spreads the evidence at gale speed. Even one ember of inconsistency becomes visible. Fresh identities need separate secure elements and counter state; a cedar tag can label the hardware record. Duplication either self-reveals or costs one hardware token per identity.
